en.name: Almonds, in shell
en.summary: Almonds in the shell keep 6 months from purchase in the cupboard, 16 months in the refrigerator, and 20 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). The shell is worth roughly double the life of a shelled kernel, because it keeps air and light off the oil.
en.pantry: A cool, dark, dry cupboard, 6 months from purchase. The shell is a genuine piece of packaging: it keeps oxygen and light away from the oil inside, which is the only thing that actually ages an almond — nothing pathogenic grows in a nut this dry. That is why in-shell almonds last about half again as long as shelled ones in the same cupboard. Keep them in a mesh bag or an open basket rather than sealed plastic, so any residual moisture in the shells can escape.
en.fridge: 16 months from purchase at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, in a sealed container. Cold slows the oxidation of the oil inside, and the shell handles the rest, which is why this figure is so much longer than for shelled kernels. Seal them properly — shells are porous and the nuts will take up fridge odours through them — and let the container come back to room temperature before opening so condensation forms on the outside rather than on the shells.
en.freezer: 20 months from purchase at −18 °C (0 °F), which is the longest figure available for any form of almond. Nuts freeze very well because they contain almost no water, so they neither go icy nor suffer texture damage. Bag them airtight with the air pressed out, and take out what you need rather than repeatedly warming a large bag — every cycle in and out brings a little moisture with it.
en.thawing: No thawing is needed. Crack and eat them straight from the freezer, or let the sealed bag reach room temperature first if you want the kernels at their crispest.
spoilage: A rancid, paint-like smell when you crack a nut open.
A bitter or soapy taste in a kernel that looks normal.
Shells with small round holes, or dust and webbing in the bag — insects.
Mould on the kernel, or a shrunken, rattling kernel inside the shell.
tips: Store in mesh or an open basket in the cupboard, not sealed plastic.
Seal them properly for the fridge or freezer — shells are porous.
Crack a few and taste before serving a batch that has been stored a long time.
Buy in shell if you want the longest life; the shell is the best packaging there is.

faq.q: How long do almonds in the shell keep?
faq.a: 6 months from purchase in the cupboard, 16 months refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 20 months frozen at −18 °C.

faq.q: Why do in-shell almonds keep longer?
faq.a: The shell keeps oxygen and light away from the oil inside, and oxidation is what actually ages a nut.

faq.q: Can you freeze almonds in the shell?
faq.a: Yes, 20 months at −18 °C (0 °F). They contain almost no water, so freezing does no harm to the texture.

zh.name: 帶殼杏仁
zh.summary: 帶殼杏仁自購買日起，放櫥櫃 6 個月、冷藏 16 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 20 個月。那層殼大約值去殼杏仁一倍的壽命，因為它把空氣和光線擋在油脂之外。
zh.pantry: 陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，自購買日起 6 個月。殼是真正有效的包裝：它把氧氣與光線隔絕在裡面的油脂之外，而氧化才是真正讓杏仁老化的原因——這麼乾的堅果不會長出什麼病原菌。這也是為什麼同一個櫥櫃裡，帶殼的比去殼的多撐大約一半的時間。請用網袋或開放式籃子存放，不要用密封塑膠袋，讓殼中殘餘的水氣能散掉。
zh.fridge: 密封容器放 4 °C 以下，自購買日起 16 個月。低溫拖慢內部油脂的氧化，殼負責其餘的部分，這就是為什麼這個數字比去殼杏仁長這麼多。密封要確實——殼是多孔的，味道會穿過去——而且容器要等回到室溫再打開，讓水氣凝在外面而不是凝在殼上。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下，自購買日起 20 個月，這是所有杏仁型態中最長的數字。堅果非常耐冷凍，因為幾乎不含水，既不會結冰晶，質地也不會受損。請用密封袋把空氣壓出，每次只取需要的量，不要反覆把一大袋回溫——每一次進出都會帶進一點水氣。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍，可以直接從冷凍取出敲開食用。想要果仁最脆，就先讓密封袋回到室溫。
spoilage: 敲開時聞到油耗味、像油漆的氣味。
外觀正常但果仁吃起來發苦或帶肥皂味。
殼上有小圓孔，或袋子裡有粉屑和絲網——有蟲。
果仁長霉，或殼裡的果仁乾縮到會晃動作響。
tips: 放櫥櫃時用網袋或開放籃，不要用密封塑膠袋。
要放冷藏或冷凍就密封確實，殼是多孔的。
存放很久的一批，先敲幾顆試味道再上桌。
想要最長的保存期就買帶殼的，殼是最好的包裝。

faq.a: 自購買日起，櫥櫃 6 個月、冷藏 4 °C 以下 16 個月、−18 °C 冷凍 20 個月。

faq.q: 為什麼帶殼的比較耐放？
faq.a: 殼把氧氣和光線擋在裡面的油脂之外，而氧化正是讓堅果老化的原因。
可以，−18 °C 下 20 個月。它幾乎不含水，冷凍不會傷害質地。

faq.q: 梅雨季帶殼杏仁還能用網袋放櫥櫃嗎？
faq.a: 乾燥的時候可以，潮濕的時候不行。殼是多孔的，濕氣一樣進得去，回潮之後裡面的仁會變軟、失去脆度，接著就是霉點。梅雨季請改成密封罐加乾燥劑，或直接冰到 4 °C 以下，那裡是 16 個月——但前提是殼本身已經乾，還帶著水氣就密封起來，等於把水關在裡面。剝開後如果殼內壁有黑點或白絮，那顆連仁一起丟。
